chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever is not forgiven in the month of Ramadan will not be forgiven until the next (Ramadan), unless he attends Arafat.

key_terms.شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ: The month of Ramadan — the ninth month of the Islamic calendar, the primary season of fasting, worship, and seeking divine forgiveness
key_terms.عَرَفَة: Arafat — the plain near Mecca where pilgrims stand on the 9th of Dhu al-Hijja, considered the spiritual peak of Hajj and a supreme moment of forgiveness
key_terms.قَابِل: The next (year); literally 'the coming one', referring to the next Ramadan

ai.seo_question: What happens if a person is not forgiven during Ramadan according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that Ramadan is the primary annual opportunity for divine forgiveness — so central that failing to attain forgiveness within it means one must wait a full year, with one exception: attending Arafat during the Hajj pilgrimage in Dhu al-Hijja. This hadith underscores the extraordinary spiritual weight of both Ramadan and the Day of Arafat (the 9th of Dhu al-Hijja), the two most elevated opportunities for forgiveness in the Islamic calendar. The early Shia community understood this as a powerful motivation to maximize worship and repentance during Ramadan.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al hakam, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who is not Forgiven in the Month of Ramazan, would not have Forgiveness for him up to the next (Month of Ramazan), except if he were to be present at Arafaat (during Zilhajj)’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn al-Hakam who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
if one is not forgiven in the month of Ramadan, one will not be forgiven until the coming month of Ramadan unless he attends ‘Arafah (the ninth of the month of Dhul Hajjah).”
